instructions: Peel the 4 bananas, which should be very ripe, and put them whole in a medium saucepan with 1/3 cup light brown sugar and 1 tbsp white wine. Cook over medium heat, turning the bananas gently, for about 3 minutes, until the sugar melts into a syrup.
Let it simmer for 5 minutes, turning the bananas once. Take the pan off the heat and leave the bananas in the syrup for 20 to 30 minutes while you do the rest.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Melt the 3 tbsp butter in a small pan over low heat.
Brush an 8 inch round cake pan with 1 tbsp of the melted butter. Add 1 tbsp sugar and tilt the pan until the bottom and sides are coated.
Tear 3.5 oz of the baguette, about a third of the loaf, into pieces the size of a pea.
In a large bowl, whisk the 2 eggs, the last 1 tbsp sugar, 1 cup coconut milk, the rest of the melted butter and 1/4 tsp salt until smooth.
Lift 2 of the bananas out of the syrup and mash them into the bowl with a fork until they're mostly smooth. Stir in the bread and leave it for 5 minutes to soak up the liquid.
Spread the batter evenly in the pan. Slice the other 2 bananas into thin coins and lay them over the top. Brush them with half the syrup.
Bake for 40 minutes, until the edges are set and the top looks dry.
Brush the top with the rest of the syrup and bake it for about 10 minutes, until it's golden. A knife in the center should come out without wet batter on it.
Let it cool in the pan for 10 minutes. Run a knife around the edge, turn it out and cut it into 8 wedges. Serve it warm or at room temperature.
method_notes: None of the banana cakes read had 20 or more ratings, and RecipeTin Eats, the trusted cook for Vietnamese, has no banh chuoi, so this follows Cooking Therapy's baguette version, the quickest of the three. All of them bind ripe bananas and bread with coconut milk, bananas first cooked or soaked in sugar and wine or rum, and bake it until golden on top. Cooking Therapy mashes half the bananas into an egg custard and lays the rest on top, What To Cook Today bakes a custard thickened with rice flour, tapioca and condensed milk covered for 90 minutes, and Helen's Recipes marinates the bananas in red wine overnight and adds raisins. Ordinary bananas stand in for the small Thai bananas in the lead, and the lead's optional coconut sauce is left off.
